thread:
maria: Heads-up — we're drafting the Redwood Private KMS integration checklist for control-plane + data-plane encryption. Need alignment on DEK caching, rotation/rewrap, RBAC (service account -> IAM role), and a fallback if KMS is unavailable. Anyone got quick wins?

aj: +1. Couple constraints: customers want BYOK, cross-account CMKs, and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. We should list required grants and test steps.

sam: For BYOK the usual pattern: customer CMK in their account; our control plane assumes a role in their account with kms:Decrypt, Encrypt, GenerateDataKey permissions. Prefer cross-account grants for short-lived ops.

maria: Agreed. Also: recommend DEK cache TTL defaults and eviction strategy. If DEK cache is too long we risk using stale keys post-rotation.

kevin: Proposed defaults: DEK_CACHE_TTL=300 (5m) for control-plane requests, allow customers to  override up to 3600s. For high-throughput data-plane, allow a separate DEK_CACHE_TTL=60 with batching.

sam: Make sure to surface rewrap hooks: when CMK rotates or we detect rewrap-required, control plane should call ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey with new CMK and mark the old DEK as archived. Have a forced rewrap job with exponential backoff.

maria: Example devops command we use in testing: 
```bash
# create a grant for the platform role in customer account
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name "redwood-grant-test"
```

kevin: For RBAC mapping: use a short-lived aws:SourceAccount + condition on aws:PrincipalArn and sts:AssumeRole session tag (customer_project). Policy snippet for CMK: 
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane"},
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:ReEncrypt*"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceAccount": "123456789012"}}
}
```

aj: We should avoid wildcard Resource on CMKs; use the key ARN. Also include EncryptionContext validation; require a customer_project tag in EncryptionContext so replays from other projects can't decrypt.

sam: Audit logging: ensure CloudTrail is enabled for kms:CreateGrant, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt. Forward those trails to customer's S3/CloudWatch or NX. In Private we should configure an option to mirror logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket.

maria: For incident response: if KMS is unavailable (region outage or service limits), plan:
1) Fail open? No — we must fail closed for plaintext.
2) Use a pre-approved emergency CMK in customer account (delegated, with very tight grant and MFA condition) to rewrap DEKs.
3) If customer consents, ephemeral fallback CMK hosted in customer account with explicit, time-limited grant to our emergency role.
4) Last-resort: disable data-plane writes and continue read-only from cached DEKs until cache TTL expires.

kevin: Ops playbook snippet for emergency rewrap: 
```text
- Notify customer via runbook channel
- Assume role: arn:aws:iam::CUST:role/redwood-emergency
- Run: aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.enc --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:alias/emer-2026 --source-encryption-context '{"project":"proj-x"}' --destination-encryption-context '{"project":"proj-x"}'
- Mark DEK as rotated, increment key version metadata
```

aj: Add tests: simulate KMS throttle (429) and region failover. Validate our retry/backoff and ensure we don't leak plaintext when re-encrypt fails. Create a chaos test in CI that kills kms endpoints.

sam: On rotation cadence: recommend default CMK rotation every 1y, but we have to support customer-triggered rotation at any time. When rotation initiated, trigger async rewrap and mark old DEKs with rotated_at and tombstone after confirmation.

maria: Quick note on DEK storage: store only encrypted DEK (ciphertext) + key metadata (key id, wrap algorithm, encryption_context) and rotate metadata pointer atomically. No plaintext DEK in any logs.

kevin: Regarding permissions for control-plane -> dataplane: split roles. control-plane role: GenerateDataKey/Encrypt for key provisioning. dataplane runtime role: only Decrypt for generating in-memory plaintext DEKs, never write to durable storage.

maria: kms-bot: can you create a checklist item in runbooks repo for the above and add a verifier job to the PR pipeline?

kms-bot: created checklist: "private-kms-integration-checklist.md" in runbooks (link: https://git.redwood/runbooks/private-kms-integration-checklist). Added CI verifier: kms-rotation-smoke.

ops-bot: FYI - filed incident playbook update ticket #SEC-7123 to add emergency CMK flow and audit forwarding.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll draft the customer-facing matrix (required IAM roles, grant samples, audit export steps, and emergency runbook) and ping infra for review.

kevin: One last ask: include a snippet to validate encryption context on decrypt call (server-side) and drop if mismatch. Small example: 
```python
def decrypt_and_validate(ciphertext, expected_context):
    resp = kms_client.decrypt(CiphertextBlob=ciphertext, EncryptionContext=expected_context)
    if resp.get('KeyId') != expected_context['key_arn']:
        raise Exception('context mismatch')
    return resp['Plaintext']
```

maria: Perfect. I'm going to schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to finalize the checklist. :thumbsup:
